summary: spectral-core 3.0.9 exfiltrates installer host files to webhook.site at npm install via binding.gyp
details: The package ships a binding.gyp with `gypfile: true` but no native sources (.c/.cc/.cpp/.h) — only an index.js stub, package.json, and binding.gyp. npm triggers `node-gyp rebuild` automatically when a binding.gyp is present, and this binding.gyp uses a GYP `type: none` target with an `action` that invokes `node -e` to execute inline JavaScript at install time. The inline payload reads `/flag.txt`, enumerates the filesystem via `find / -name flag*`, `ls -la /output/`, `cat /output/*`, `/etc/hosts`, and `/proc/mounts`, and POSTs the collected contents to https://webhook.site/f604623f-fc78-4447-9225-6772f7f12cb1. Because no real native addon is built, the binding.gyp exists solely to carry this install-time execution and exfiltration payload. The package name resembles the legitimate Stoplight `@stoplight/spectral-core`, consistent with a typosquat lure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
